Why: The statement conveys a negative near-term outlook due to COVID-19 disruptions, but it pairs this with aggressive easing—zeroing the policy rate, restarting large-scale Treasury and MBS purchases, expanding repos, cutting the discount rate, and activating global dollar swap lines. The credit-channel literature (e.g., Kashyap, Lamont, and Stein; Gertler and Gilchrist; Oliner and Rudebusch) suggests these actions can lower external finance premia and support investment and household spending, mitigating downturns. With market-based inflation compensation falling and inflation below target, easing is consistent with research on deflation risk and expectations management (central bank credibility and inflation-forecast targeting). At the effective lower bound/liquidity-trap risk, nontraditional tools become pivotal (as highlighted in monetary policy frameworks such as McCallum–Nelson), so the commitment to use the “full range of tools” meaningfully offsets the otherwise negative tone.

Most important sentence: "The Federal Reserve is prepared to use its full range of tools to support the flow of credit to households and businesses..."
